_comment: Concentric-view anchors. The root is a wave propagating outward; everything in this file is constructed in sync_cost/curriculum/01_what_a_wave_is. The six observations are planted (un-named) at the end of that module and named in the (not-yet-written) Module 1a. Each link's `tier` records derivation strength against the substrate: T1 = framework constructs this observation (or a clean substrate analog) from primitives; T2 = framework engages with it / makes predictions involving it but does not derive it; T3 = textbook landmark with no constructive substrate engagement (link is analog or category-match only). Audited 2026-06-29 against derivation-graph.json (commit f4b9a80).

T1.label: derived
T1.description: The framework constructs this observation (or a clean substrate analog) from its primitives. The linked doc does load-bearing constructive work for this anchor.

T2.label: engaged
T2.description: The framework engages with this observation, makes predictions involving it, or uses it as a parameter — but does not derive it from substrate primitives.

T3.label: imported
T3.description: Textbook landmark with no constructive substrate engagement. The link is an analog or category-match, not a derivation. Listed here in honesty about what the framework does and does not do.

root.label: wave outward
root.summary: A disturbance propagating from one point to another through a medium with restoring tendency, inertia, and coupling between neighbors. The single object every claim in this graph descends from.

ingredients.label: restoration
ingredients.summary: Near any rest state, the energy is locally a parabola; the restoring force is proportional to displacement. Forced by the local-parabola role planted in Module 0.

ingredients.label: inertia
ingredients.summary: Mass means the medium overshoots when restored. Without it, no oscillation. With it, period 2π·√(m/k).

ingredients.label: coupling
ingredients.summary: A force between neighbors that responds to their *relative* displacement. Translation symmetry of the medium forces this form. What turns a row of oscillators into a wave.

observations.label: Doppler shift
observations.tier_note: The framework has no constructive Doppler derivation. Its only frequency-shift content is intra-substrate arithmetic (FM beat / CRT composition), which is structurally different — coupling changes the wave, not observer motion. Kept here in honesty about the gap.
observations.summary: Relative motion between source and observer shifts the measured frequency. Textbook. The framework's nearest substrate analog is FM-beat arithmetic, which composes modes by frequency difference but does not involve motion through a medium.

links.relation: analog only — composite modes as differences of primitive modes, bounded by Mihailescu; not observer-motion shift

observations.label: redshift
observations.tier_note: Framework treats redshift z as a coordinate (input from ΛCDM) and makes predictions parametric in it; does not derive cosmic redshift from substrate.
observations.summary: The cosmic-scale version of frequency shift: distant sources, receding as the cosmos stretches, are measured at lower frequencies. The shift grows with distance.

links.relation: canonical cosmological power-spectrum tilt from mode-locking structure (the non-superseded version)
a₀(z) = cH(z)/(2π) prediction parametric in z; redshift consumed as input

observations.label: time dilation
observations.tier_note: Strong derivation: GR (and thus geometric time dilation) falls out of the Kuramoto continuum limit at K=1.
observations.summary: If a wave's propagation speed is the same for every observer, time and distance must be measured differently by different observers. The wave's constancy forces the geometry.

links.relation: Einstein field equations derived as unique K=1 continuum output (Lovelock 1971)
ADM evolution + Hamiltonian/momentum constraints → Einstein equations at σ²=1/4
Christoffel/Levi-Civita connection emerges in continuum limit; Γ̃ = Γ + O(1/N)

observations.label: E = mc²
observations.tier_note: Framework derives mass values and ratios from substrate (integer conservation law, generation structure) but does not construct the inertia↔energy equivalence as such.
observations.summary: A wave confined to a small region carries energy proportional to its frequency of confinement. That confined energy, pinned in place, is what we call mass.

links.relation: integer law depth × |3Q| = k_sector with k_lepton = q₃² = 9, k_quark = q₂³ = 8

observations.label: Planck wall
observations.tier_note: Strong derivation. The Planck scale is constructed as a self-sustaining substrate threshold (N=3, three-stage ℏ↔c↔G loop), and the Planck-Hubble hierarchy ratio is derived to 0.48%.
observations.summary: The smallest-scale wall. Below this confinement scale, the energy required to localize the wave makes its own gravitational horizon. No wave can be defined further in.

links.relation: R = q₂q₃ · (q₂² + q₃²)^(q₂q₃^d) = 6 · 13^54 matches t_H/t_P to 0.48%
Planck scale as N=3 self-sustaining threshold of the substrate

observations.label: Hubble wall
observations.tier_note: Strong derivation at the hierarchy end (paired with the Planck wall in the same ratio); the cosmological-cycle structure engages the Hubble regime constructively.
observations.summary: The largest-scale wall. Above this wavelength, the cosmos stretches faster than the wave can complete a cycle. No wave can complete a coherent oscillation further out.

links.relation: the Hubble end of the derived t_H/t_P ratio
engages the Hubble-scale regime structurally; reads the wall as part of the cycle's outer turn
MOND threshold a₀ = cH₀/(2π); H₀ as anchor parameter

our_band.label: where we live
our_band.summary: Our frequency — sound, light, chemistry, biology — sits decades-deep between the two walls. The behavior at our frequency is extremely stable because we are far from both boundaries; no boundary correction matters at our scale. The framework's dramatic moves happen at the walls; here, locally, the construction simply holds.
